blocks.html: He was therefore a false attorney; for so is called, in our law, not only he who has never had, either before or after, charge from the person whose attorney he says he is a, or indeed who once had it but has had it revoked, as he well knew b; but also he who has overstepped the ends and bounds of his power, or who had no charge at the time of the execution c; nay, even he who had been well and legitimately appointed, if he did not know it and nevertheless did the acts of an attorney d. True it is that in this case Pierre Guerre, a false attorney at the beginning, has been ratified by the said de Rols, and so all that had been done by him was confirmed and approved e; considering singularly that the acts of attorney done by the said Guerre, before the charge or procuration of the said de Rols, were done by authority of the Judge of Rieux — which comes into some consideration: for if they had been done by authority of the Court, that might have admitted of some doubt, inasmuch as the law holds in such great horror and detestation obreption, and a fault committed in the consistory of the prince f, that what is done by a false attorney in the audience-chamber of the prince cannot (as many think) be confirmed by any subsequent ratification g,

notes.citation: Digest 12.4 (De condictione causa data causa non secuta), l. Si procuratori falso (fragment not identified), and Accursius (Accurse) there; Code 2.12 (De procuratoribus), l. Licet (law not identified)
notes.original: l. ſi procura tori falſo. & i lec Accurſe, D. de cõd. ca. dau. l. licet. C. de procu.
notes.gloss: On one who has never had the mandate of the person he claims to represent; what is paid to a false procurator may be recovered.

notes.citation: Decretals, c. Ex parte decani, under a title printed de re. (perhaps De rescriptis, X 1.3, the title of note g; chapter not identified)
notes.original: c. ex parte Decani. de re.
notes.gloss: The procurator whose mandate has been revoked, and who knows it.

notes.citation: Code 6.2 (De furtis), l. Falsus (law not identified), and the Gloss and the Doctors there; the Gloss and the Masters on c. Ex parte (as note b)
notes.original: l ſulſus. & il lac les gloſe & docteurs. C. de fur. la Glo & les maiſtres au c. ex parte.
notes.gloss: The print's ſulſus is a wrong sort for falſus, the law Baldus is cited on at note g. The procurator who exceeds his mandate, or has none at the time he acts.

notes.citation: Digest 27.5.3 (De eo qui pro tutore prove curatore negotia gessit, l. Quaero; Javolenus, on one named tutor by will who acts without knowing it); Digest 46.7.3.5 (Iudicatum solvi, l. 3, § Sed et si quidem; Ulpian)
notes.original: l. quæro. D. de eo qui pro tutor. l. iij. Ꝑ.⟨alt?:P.⟩ ſed & ſi quidem. D. Iud. ſol.
notes.gloss: One who acts as guardian or procurator without knowing he has been appointed is treated as acting without mandate.

notes.citation: Digest 5.1.56 (De iudiciis, l. Licet; Ulpian: Licet verum procuratorem in iudicio rem deducere verissimum est…, the principal's ratification cures the false procurator's joinder of issue); Digest 46.8.3.1 (Ratam rem haberi et de ratihabitione, l. 3, § Falsus)
notes.original: l. licet. D. de Iud. l. iij. P. fal ſus. D. rem ra. hab.
notes.gloss: Ratification by the principal cures the acts of a false procurator: ratihabitio mandato comparatur.

notes.citation: Code 7.10.7 (De his qui a non domino manumissi sunt), the last law of the title — a constitution of Constantine, not Justinian (§ 1: he who manumits another's slave in the emperor's presence, fallendo principis conscientiam, is fined two slaves to the owner and three to the fisc)
notes.original: l. finale. C. de ius qui à nõ do. man.
notes.gloss: The print's de ius qui is de iis qui. Cited for the law's severity towards a fraud practised in the emperor's consistory.

notes.citation: Baldus (Balde) on Code 6.2.19 (De furtis, l. Falsus, as note c); Panormitanus (Panorme, Niccolò de' Tudeschi) on Decretals X 1.3.28 (De rescriptis, c. Nonnulli), § 1 Sunt et alii
notes.original: Balde en la l. falſus. C. de fur. Panorme au c. nonnulli. P. ſunt & a iij. de reſcrip.
notes.gloss: The print's a iij. is read as alij. On rescripts and acts obtained in the prince's court by obreption, which, in the opinion Coras reports, no later ratification can confirm.
